recall_formula: recall@k = |relevant ∩ top-k| / |relevant|, averaged over the 20 queries (matches src-tauri/benches/memory_quality.rs)
note: Each framework was run for real through its OWN retriever on the same corpus + the same embedder. Numbers cluster tightly because the embedder, not the framework, sets vector recall — plain vector RAG is plumbing around the same embeddings. TerranSoul's vectors in memory_quality.json are the bench's deterministic stand-in, so this compares retrieval STRATEGY (plain vector vs TerranSoul's hybrid+RRF), not embedders. GraphRAG is tracked separately (graph/community retrieval returns synthesized context, not a document ranking).

systems.via: ragflow-sdk 0.22.1 -> RAGFlow.retrieve() (self-hosted Docker: ragflow-cpu + elasticsearch + mysql + redis + minio; ES vector retriever, nomic-embed-text 768-dim)
llama-index-core VectorStoreIndex + OllamaEmbedding(nomic-embed-text), as_retriever(similarity_top_k=20), MockLLM (retrieval only)

graphrag 3.1.0 `index --method fast` (extract_graph_nlp, no per-doc LLM) + local search context builder; nomic-embed-text embeddings; ~2m15s index. Full detail + per-query evidence in rag_graphrag_bench.json.
systems.note: Unblocked via the fast indexing method (the earlier ~67-min LLM-extraction blocker is gone). Low + flat R@k is a METRIC MISMATCH, not a failure: GraphRAG local search returns a small entity-focused context (<=5 sources/query) for answer synthesis, not a broad top-20 ranking — so recall@k-over-documents understates it. Read as 'different tool', not '8x worse'.
